name: Pediatric lateral or medial parapatellar arthrotomy
region: pediatric anterior knee and distal femur
corridor: Limited parapatellar capsular incision adjacent to the patellar tendon, selected on the fracture side

positioning.text: Position supine on a radiolucent table with the knee freely flexed and the injured side of the joint accessible.

setup.text: Review CT or MRI when needed to define the epiphyseal fracture, choose the side that best exposes the target, and prepare fluoroscopy and physeal-respecting fixation.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark patella, patellar-tendon borders, joint line, tibial tubercle, and involved femoral condyle.

incision.text: Begin beside the patellar tendon at midpatellar level and extend initially to the joint line; lengthen only as required for articular reduction.

superficial_interval.text: Develop a limited parapatellar tract without broad skin flaps or unnecessary extensor-mechanism stripping.

deep_interval.text: Incise capsule in the skin-incision plane and use gentle retractors for direct fracture visualization; keep sharp dissection away from the meniscus.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue, parapatellar retinacular-capsular layer, synovium, then articular fracture.

structures_encountered.text: Patellar tendon, retinaculum, capsule, synovium, meniscus, femoral condyle, physis, and epiphyseal fragment may be encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: Meniscus, articular cartilage, patellar tendon, infrapatellar saphenous branches medially, and the distal-femoral physis are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Avoid sharp dissection around the meniscus and repeated manipulation across the injured physis.

retraction_hazards.text: Use small blunt retractors under direct vision and avoid levering on pediatric cartilage or the patellar tendon.

exposure.text: Provides targeted direct visualization of the selected femoral condyle and articular surface with limited soft-tissue disruption.

limitations.text: The limited window is inadequate for complex bicondylar or posterior fractures that cannot be reduced under direct vision.

extensions.text: Lengthen proximally or distally along the chosen parapatellar side when additional articular visualization is necessary.

indications.text: Use for selected pediatric articular and epiphyseal fractures needing limited direct reduction and fixation.

relative_contraindications.text: Choose a broader lateral, medial, or extensile parapatellar exposure when the fracture cannot be visualized and controlled through a limited arthrotomy.

implant_implications.text: Place implants under direct and fluoroscopic control to restore the joint while minimizing avoidable physeal and cartilage violation.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Use orthogonal and tangential views to verify articular congruity, physeal alignment, trajectory, and implant containment.

closure.text: Repair the capsule with absorbable suture after hemostasis, then close subcutaneous tissue and skin routinely.

complications.text: Complications include meniscal or chondral injury, growth arrest, stiffness, infection, malreduction, and fixation failure.

bailouts.text: Extend or convert the exposure when fracture visualization remains inadequate rather than performing blind reduction or fixation.

procedure_applications.condition: A pediatric epiphyseal or articular fracture requires direct visualization through a limited medial or lateral parapatellar window

questions.question: Where does the initial incision run?
questions.answer: Adjacent to the patellar tendon from midpatella to the joint line.

questions.question: What structure must sharp dissection avoid?
When is the incision extended?
questions.answer: When more articular exposure is needed for reduction and fixation.
